notes: SHIP v1.14.369 - OPS WALL TILE RASTERS RE-CUT AT 384. Owner ruling: 384, ship as .369. The ART-DROP-OPS-WALL package (12 files, sha256 verified 12 of 12 against its own manifest) supersedes the 1024 batch that .367 downscaled. WHY 384 AND NOT 256: .368 squared the cell (aspect-ratio 1/1). The wall is a 3-column grid, 8px gap inside 10px padding, so at a 390pt shell each cell is about 108px CSS. On a 3x iPhone that is about 324 device pixels against a 256px raster - the live tiles were under-resolved by roughly a quarter, which is exactly the detail the 1254 regens carry. 384 covers 3x with headroom. SCOPE: seven raster files, nothing else. No markup, no CSS, no precache edit, no DEPLOY_TOOLS, no sample data. The cells take their art through the --tim custom property as a background-image, so a raster dimension change needs no markup change by construction. FILENAMES ARE DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, which is why sw.js had to move: an unchanged URL whose bytes changed is served from the old cache indefinitely, so the CACHE_VERSION bump is the ONLY thing pushing these to a device. That is .367s lesson restated. WHAT MOVED: bom, manifest, rackmap, sops, burndown, audits (phantom-tool-*-256.webp) and optics (phantom-ref-optics-256.webp - note the ref- prefix; it is the one tile off the tool- pattern and the easy one to miss). WHAT DID NOT MOVE, AND WHY: PORT MAP still carries the 1024 JPEG placeholder, because the drop ships it as temp with a family-style regen prompt still open. BLAST still carries phantom-tool-power-256.webp, because no family-style BLAST render exists yet (drop open item 2). Both are known gaps, not oversights - the wall reads as seven crisp tiles and two softer ones until they land. NAMING DEBT ACCEPTED: the files keep their -256 suffix while carrying 384px content. A rename would mean fourteen reference edits across dct-ios.html and sw.js PRECACHE for zero user-visible gain and a real orphan-reference risk on a 48.5k-line file, so it was not taken on unasked. Flagged for an owner ruling as its own pass. ENCODE: sharp 0.35.3 / libwebp 1.6.0, lanczos3 downscale 1254 to 384, quality 82 / alphaQuality 95 / effort 6 - the drops locked cwebp -q 82 -alpha_q 95 -m 6 spec, same libwebp knobs. No cwebp, sharp or ImageMagick existed on the build box; the encoder was installed to scratchpad, not to the repo or globally. Note /c/Windows/system32/convert is the Windows FAT converter, not ImageMagick. PRECACHE COST: the seven tiles go from about 124KB to about 212KB total, +88KB. BATCH: this is the 6th stacked ship (.364 through .369) and TRIPS THE CALL 0 CAP - the consolidated BATCH-VERIFY pass is due before any further ship. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) fully quit the PWA and relaunch, badge reads v1.14.369 - a soft reopen serves the old cache and will read as a failed ship. (2) STAND-BACK TEST on the OPS wall: seven tiles visibly sharper, PORT MAP and BLAST visibly softer by comparison - that contrast is the proof the swap landed. (3) Both shells. (4) All nine cells must still tap through; art must never cost a door. (5) Watch OPTICS bottom-left, where the corner text lands on bright slabs. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - restores the .367 rasters with every door, binding and precache entry intact.
